smt-2019-general-tiebreaker-01.title: Exponents of 2 and 3
smt-2019-general-tiebreaker-01.body:
$216=2^3\cdot3^3$, and $\operatorname{lcm}(x,y)=216$ means $x,y\mid216$ and, for each prime, the larger of the two exponents is $3$. For the prime $2$, the exponent pairs $(i,j)$ with $0\le i,j\le3$ and $\max(i,j)=3$ number $4\cdot4-3\cdot3=7$. The same holds for the prime $3$. The choices are independent, so there are $7\cdot7=49$ ordered pairs $(x,y)$.

**Answer: 49**

smt-2019-general-tiebreaker-02.title: Trapezoid area and Pythagoras
smt-2019-general-tiebreaker-02.body:
The circles are tangent, so $O_1O_2=R+r$. $A$ and $B$ are the tangency points of the external tangent, so $O_1A$ and $O_2B$ are radii perpendicular to $AB$ (parallel to each other): $ABO_1O_2$ is a right trapezoid with parallel sides $R,r$ and height $AB=16$. Its area is $\frac{16(R+r)}{2}=160$, so $R+r=20$.

Dropping a perpendicular from $O_2$ to $O_1A$ gives a right triangle with legs $R-r$ and $16$ and hypotenuse $O_1O_2=R+r$: $(R-r)^2+16^2=(R+r)^2$, so $4Rr=256$, $Rr=64$. With $R+r=20$: $R-r=\sqrt{400-256}=12$, so $R=16$, $r=4$.

**Answer: $(r,R)=(4,16)$**

smt-2019-general-tiebreaker-03.title: Count appearances
smt-2019-general-tiebreaker-03.body:
Each element of $S$ lies in exactly $2^{10}=1024$ subsets, so the total is $1024\cdot(1+3+\dots+21)=1024\cdot11^2=1024\cdot121=123904$ (the sum of the first $11$ odd numbers is $11^2$).

**Answer: 123904**
